extracted.intended_audience: developers and users who want to run or reproduce 3Blue1Brown manim-generated scenes (manim/manimgl users)
extracted.subtask_description: Instructions and workflow for installing dependencies, configuring an editor (Sublime), and running or interactively debugging the manim-generated scenes used in 3Blue1Brown videos. Covers required packages, repository usage, interactive commands, and keybindings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the 3b1b/manim fork (compatibility)
rubrics_metrics.description: Note that I'm using 3b1b/manim, not the community edition; some functionality may differ between the two.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Older projects may depend on older versions of manim and so may not run out of the box. If you use the community edition or a different manim version, expect incompatibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Install manimgl from source
rubrics_metrics.description: Install manimgl from source since the latest version published is not up to date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The README explicitly recommends building manimgl from source to match the code in this repository rather than relying on a possibly outdated published package.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure LaTeX is installed
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure LaTeX is installed (examples given for Ubuntu).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: On Ubuntu install texlive, texlive-latex-extra, texlive-fonts-extra, texlive-science using: sudo apt install texlive sudo apt install texlive-latex-extra sudo apt install texlive-fonts-extra sudo apt install texlive-science. LaTeX is required for LaTeX-rendered text in scenes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clone repository to run examples
rubrics_metrics.description: Clone this repository to run the video samples: git clone git@github.com:3b1b/videos.git; cd videos
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work in the repository tree (examples live under dated folders like _2023/optics_puzzles).

rubrics_metrics.name: Run a scene or file with manimgl
rubrics_metrics.description: Run a video or specific scene with manimgl using: manimgl <file> or manimgl <file> <SceneName> (example: manimgl e_field.py or manimgl e_field.py WavesIn3D).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the basic non-interactive way to render scenes to view or to produce output files.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use interactive mode for debugging (-se with line number)
rubrics_metrics.description: Running manimgl (file name) (scene name) -se (line_number) will drop you into an interactive mode at that line of the file, with an iPython terminal usable to interact with the scene.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interactive mode acts like a debugger, letting you inspect and modify the scene state. This is central to the author's workflow.

rubrics_metrics.name: checkpoint_paste() semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: Within the interactive mode, entering "checkpoint_paste()" will run whatever bit of code is copied to the clipboard. If that copied code begins with a comment, the first time it sees that comment it will save the state of the scene at that point, and for all future calls on code beginning with the same comment, it will first revert to that state of the scene before running the code.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 'skip' argument of checkpoint_paste will run the code without animating (as if run times set to 0). The 'record' argument will cause animations run with that copied code to be rendered to file. Use these modes to quickly iterate or to produce renders from the interactive workflow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Set up Sublime integration (Terminus + custom commands)
rubrics_metrics.description: Install Terminus (via package control) to get an in-editor terminal, then copy files from the sublime_custom_commands sub-directory into Packages/User/ to enable custom commands that interact with manimgl and the editor state.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Terminus lets plugins take the state in Sublime (cursor location, selection) and run desired command-line instructions. Copying the provided custom commands into Packages/User/ mimics the author's Sublime setup.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommended Sublime keybindings and behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: Add keybindings to call the custom commands (example keybindings provided: shift+super+r -> manim_run_scene, super+r -> manim_checkpoint_paste, super+alt+r -> manim_recorded_checkpoint_paste, super+ctrl+r -> manim_skipped_checkpoint_paste, super+e -> manim_exit, super+option+/ -> comment_fold).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Behavioral notes: manim_run_scene drops you into interactive mode at the cursor's scene line; if the cursor is on the scene-defining line it copies the render command to the clipboard. manim_checkpoint_paste copies highlighted code then runs checkpoint_paste() in the interactive terminal. Customize keys as you prefer.

rubrics_metrics.name: How manim_run_scene decides what to run
rubrics_metrics.description: If the cursor is inside a line of a scene, manim_run_scene will drop you into interactive mode at that point of the scene. If the cursor is on the line defining the scene, it will copy to the clipboard the command needed to render that full scene to file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This explains the UX of the provided Sublime command: context-sensitive behavior depending on cursor location.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adjust sys.path for example imports
rubrics_metrics.description: When running an example, add to the top of the file sys.path.append("."), sys.path.append(".."), sys.path.append("../..") so imports resolve when executing examples from their folder.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example given: cd _2023/optics_puzzles; vi e_field.py and add those sys.path.append lines near the top to make relative imports work when invoking manimgl from that directory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generalizable workflow for non-Sublime editors
rubrics_metrics.description: If you use another text editor, the same functionality can be mimicked: the key idea is using an editor-integrated terminal and commands that use editor state (cursor/selection) to run the appropriate manimgl commands or checkpoint_paste flows.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The README emphasizes the two key facts (interactive manimgl mode and checkpoint_paste semantics) which are portable; users of other editors should recreate similar shortcuts/plugins to achieve the same workflow.
